metric: Physiological stress markers (EEG power, HR, HRV, respiration) and user preference between two tactile breathing devices
result: No significant difference in mean HR between devices; HRV decreased with both during use; moonbird produced more sustained EEG/respiratory effects and was preferred overall for handling and breathing guidance (no preference or effect-size numbers reported)

metric: Three-class cognitive load classification accuracy from multimodal physiological signals (EEG, EDA, ECG, EOG, eye movements) during flight-relevant tasks
result: Average classification accuracy 81.08% and F1-score 80.94% across 22 participants using a multiview feature-selection framework

metric: Mental workload assessment via subjective, physiological (EEG, ECG, EDA, eye movement), and driving-performance measures during simulated dual-task driving
result: Increasing secondary-task difficulty raised subjective workload and reduced secondary-task performance; ECG time/frequency-domain measures and other physiological/driving indices showed workload-related changes (no effect sizes reported)

metric: Association between ECG/PPG-derived heart rate response to a cognitive 1-back task and depression/anxiety severity
result: Task accuracy decreased with difficulty; heart-rate increases under cognitive load were associated with higher depression/trait-anxiety (PPG) and with anxiety attacks (ECG), an association that weakened at higher difficulty (no effect sizes reported)

metric: Mental workload detection accuracy from a 3-channel EEG (gamma-band) model in air traffic controllers, using mRMR channel selection
result: Detection rate of 1.0 for 34 subjects and accuracy as low as 0.986 for the remaining subjects (total sample size not stated)

metric: Correlation between intraoperative heart rate variability and surgeons' self-reported stress (STAI-6) during vascular surgery
result: HRV indicated greater stress at key procedural points across 11 surgeons; HRV correlated with subjective stress (r=0.768, p<0.001)

metric: Feasibility and usability of a multimodal sensor-based (eye-tracking, ECG chest strap, motion) eHealth intervention for pediatric OCD therapy
result: Technology was well accepted; patients, parents, and therapists reported high satisfaction and fewer OCD symptoms at treatment end (no numeric satisfaction score reported)

error_rate: 0 adverse events reported (0/17 patients) over 9 hours of device wear
metric: Safety (adverse events), feasibility (data capture), and acceptability (comfort/satisfaction) of a wearable EEG/ECG device for monitoring ischaemic stroke patients
result: No adverse events among 17 patients wearing the device for 9 hours, only minor discomfort; comfort and data-capture feasibility were assessed at 1, 3, 6, and 9 hours but exact values are not present in this abstract excerpt

error_rate: Mean absolute error <1 bpm (HR) and 6-15 ms (HRV); HRV relative error 14-51% higher during activity than at rest
metric: Accuracy of PPG-derived heart rate (HR) and heart rate variability (HRV) versus an ECG reference sensor in free-living conditions
result: Mean absolute error <1 bpm for HR and 6-15 ms for HRV; PPG HRV error 14-51% higher during activity than rest; peak-detection F1 score of 89% during sleep, across 25 volunteers monitored for 10 days

metric: Accuracy of a 2-stage hierarchical ECG classification model for biometric user identification across varying stress states
result: Identification accuracy of 92.08% (CSU-BIODB) and 95.83% (MIT-BIH ST Change database); F1 scores of 0.9207 and 0.9369; 9.3% and 36.76% accuracy improvement over single-stage baseline models

metric: Effect of citrus odour on cognitive performance (2-back task) and autonomic measures (ECG/HRV, PPG, EDA) under cognitive load
result: Citrus odour significantly improved 2-back accuracy and suppressed the EDA rise seen under cognitive load; parasympathetic HRV measures (pNN50, RMSSD, HF power) increased, though overall HRV variability was unchanged (no effect sizes reported)

error_rate: Accuracy root-mean-square (ARMS) of 1.67 bpm under no-motion conditions
metric: Accuracy of a machine-learning wrist-worn PPG continuous pulse-rate algorithm versus a reference ECG device
result: ARMS of 1.67 bpm under no-motion conditions across 16,915 paired observations from 157 subjects in 3 clinical trials, meeting the pre-specified acceptance thresholds (<=3 bpm no-motion, <=5 bpm motion)

metric: Accuracy of a deep-learning modular ECG algorithm, with a cardiologist-adjudication interface, for atrial fibrillation/flutter detection on long-term Holter recordings
result: F1 scores of 99% (atrial tachyarrhythmia), 95% (atrial fibrillation), and 90% (atrial flutter) on 187 internal recordings (249,419 samples); external MIT-BIH validation F1 97% (normal sinus rhythm) and 96% (tachyarrhythmia); residual errors correctable by manual module deactivation in 7 of 15 lower-accuracy recordings

metric: Correlation between heart rate variability (pRR50%) and aerobic fitness (20 m shuttle test) versus heart rate alone, during police tactical selection
result: pRR50% significantly correlated with shuttle-test performance (rho=0.812, p=0.050); heart rate alone was not significantly correlated with fitness or predictive of task performance, across a cohort of 6 candidates
